blocks.text: Imagine you have a list of numbers and you need to find the median. Sorting the entire list seems excessive. Is there a faster way?

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we explore the problem of finding the $k$th smallest element in an unsorted list. This problem is known as the selection problem. We will learn about the Quickselect algorithm, which efficiently solves this problem using a divide-and-conquer approach.

blocks.title: Selection Problem
blocks.text: The selection problem involves finding the $k$th smallest element in an unsorted list of numbers.

blocks.markdown: A naive approach to solve the selection problem is to sort the list and then select the $k$th element. However, sorting has a time complexity of $O(n \log n)$. We aim for a more efficient solution.

blocks.title: Quickselect Algorithm
blocks.text: Quickselect is an algorithm to find the $k$th smallest element in expected linear time, $O(n)$, using a partitioning method similar to Quicksort.

blocks.markdown: Quickselect works by choosing a pivot and partitioning the list into elements less than the pivot and elements greater than the pivot. Depending on the position of the pivot, the algorithm recursively selects from the appropriate partition.

blocks.caption: Recurrence relation for Quickselect in the average case.

blocks.title: Finding the 3rd smallest element
blocks.prompt: Use Quickselect to find the 3rd smallest element in the list [7, 10, 4, 3, 20, 15].

steps.text: Choose a pivot. Let's say pivot is 7.
Partition the list into elements less than 7 and greater than 7.
Since 7 is the 3rd element in the partitioned list, it is the 3rd smallest element.

blocks.markdown: While Quickselect is efficient on average, its worst-case time complexity is $O(n^2)$, similar to Quicksort's worst case. To address this, we can use the median-of-medians algorithm to ensure linear time complexity in the worst case.

blocks.title: Median-of-Medians
blocks.text: The median-of-medians algorithm selects a good pivot to guarantee $O(n)$ worst-case time complexity for selection.

blocks.title: Median-of-Medians Example
blocks.prompt: Explain how the median-of-medians algorithm can be used to select a pivot.

steps.text: Divide the list into groups of 5 and find the median of each group.
Use Quickselect recursively to find the median of these medians.
Use this median as the pivot for partitioning.

blocks.answer: The median-of-medians ensures a good pivot choice, leading to $O(n)$ worst-case complexity.

points: Quickselect uses partitioning to find the $k$th smallest element in expected linear time.
Median-of-medians guarantees linear time complexity even in the worst case.
Sorting is a less efficient method for selection compared to direct algorithms.
